Order 
Learned High Court Government Pleader accepts notice for the respondent No.1-State.
Smt. Roopa B.M., learned counsel filed vakalath to appear on behalf of respondent No.2.

This petition is filed by the petitioners-accused Nos.1 and 2 under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the criminal proceedings in C.C.No.4845/2023 arising out of Crime No.183/2022 registered by East Zone Women Police Station, Bengaluru and charge sheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 420, 120(B), 504 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the D.P. Act.
2.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
During pendency of the petition, both petitioners and respondent No.2 appeared before the Court along with their counsels and filed joint compromise application on NC: 2024:KHC:10321 I.A.No.1/2024 under Section 320 read with Section 482 of Cr.P.C. along with joint affidavit seeking permission of this Court to compound the offences and also submits that the matter has been settled between them and the divorce has been granted in M.C.No.6712/2021.
3.
As per the settlement, petitioner No.1 has agreed to pay Rs.3,50,000/- to respondent No.2 towards permanent alimony.
The amount of Rs.2,50,000/- is already paid by petitioner No.1 and remaining amount of Rs.1,00,000/- paid today by way of D.D.

The same is received and acknowledged by the learned counsel for respondent No.2.
4.
Submission of both the parties are placed on record.
5. As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and Another reported in 2012 CRI.L.J.4934

Hence, I.A.No.1/2024 is allowed.
The parties are permitted to compound the offences.
